items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: Kelce's 11-yard touchdown answered Miami's opening punch and put Kansas City back in front.
items.reason: Nearest subject is Kelce (KC). Miami is the club being answered, not the scoring team.

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: Kansas City answered Miami's 3-yard touchdown, then the drive stalled.
items.reason: Clause subject of the claim is Miami, not Kansas City.

items.label: false-positive

items.reason: 10 is a KC TD. Binding must not take Miami from after the claim.

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: Rice's 88-yard run was a long gain, not a scoring play.
items.reason: Yardage is a scoring claim only with TD/touchdown or field-goal wording.

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: Kelce's 11-yard catch answered Miami in the fourth.
items.reason: A catch is not a scoring claim without TD/touchdown wording.

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: The 37-yard field goal kept Kansas City from a two-score cushion until Patterson was named.
items.reason: Unbound FG yardage 37 is on the ESPN FG list (Patterson / MIA).

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: It was a 0-0 game until Walker found the edge.
items.reason: 0-0 is a real game state (kickoff / any tie), not an invented score.

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: The two early Kansas City touchdowns set a 14-7 first-half lead.
items.reason: Qualified count is not a whole-game total. First-half KC TDs are 2 (Q1+Q2).

items.label: false-positive
items.sentence: Kansas City lost 18-19 on first downs and still won the scoreboard.
items.reason: Bare lost/won X-Y is volume (first downs), not a game-score claim. Score order is also irrelevant when a pair does match an ESPN score-after.
